items.full_text_snippet: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> 周鸿祎发布纳米Work：新一代企业智能体工作平台，为企业而生 量子位的朋友们 2026-07-29 09:53:15 来源： 量子位 7月28日，360集团创始人周鸿祎正式发布新一代企业智能体工作平台“纳米Work”。纳米Work为企业AI化而生，面向企业老板、创业者及一人公司（OPC）和企业员工，打造超级组织。发布会现场，周鸿祎提出一个鲜明的观点：企业搞AI，老板要先用。他同时宣布为首批用户每人提供1亿Token试用额度，通过专业实训和陪跑服务，率先帮助1000家小企业完成AI落地和经营提效。 周鸿祎透露，发布产品前，360先把自己作为“试验场”，将OpenClaw等各类智能体投入公司1000多个真实业务场景，收集56000多条用户反馈意见，在5个月内优化迭代166个版本后，最终推出纳米Work。他表示，纳米Work不是对某一款智能体的简单封装，而是希望将复杂技术能力隐藏起来，将先进能力转化为用户可直接使用的生产力，同时融入原生安全能力。 据了解，智能体落地企业过程中面临挑战：复杂任务可能带来不可预估的Token消耗，普通用户需要面对环境配置、模型选择、工具连接等门槛，而企业更加关注权限边界、任务稳定性以及数据安全。周鸿祎表示，智能体真正进入工作场景，需要同时解决成本、门槛、权限、稳定性、安全性和持续进化等问题。 针对这些挑战，纳米Work构建了多智能体引擎、多模型底座、云端办公室、多工作模式和多专家五大能力体系。用户无需研究模型、智能体框架和工具，只需提出目标，平台即可根据任务需求组织不同AI专家协同工作，并匹配合适的模型和执行方式。企业老板可以借助纳米Work辅助经营分析、业务增长和进度管理；创业者及一人公司可以完成机会发现、产品验证、内容生产和营销获客；企业员工则可以利用AI提升资料研究、方案策划、内容制作和项目交付效率，成为职场精英。 企业智能体要进入真实工作场景，首先必须解决安全问题。周鸿祎表示：“大模型出错，是说错话；智能体出错，是干错事。”针对智能体执行任务带来的新安全挑战，360将“原生安全、出厂内置”作为纳米Work设计原则，通过云端隔离、权限控制、数据保护等安全机制，降低企业使用AI过程中的风险，让企业敢于把真实工作交给AI。 发布会现场，新疆喀什网红早餐店”香香手”的老板阿布拉江来到现场，分享了借助纳米Work做品牌营销、做店铺设计、做法务咨询推动店铺扩张的经验。从一家早餐店发展到6家门店，阿布拉江的实践展现了AI正在进入更多普通创业者的真实经营场景。 周鸿祎认为，AI正在进入“模型与智能体双线进化”的阶段，“模型决定AI有多聪明，智能体决定AI能不能真正干活”。未来企业竞争不仅取决于模型能力，更取决于能否将模型、知识、工具和业务流程结合起来，形成稳定的任务交付能力。 同时，360启动纳米Work城市合伙人招募，进一步完善本地化服务和落地支持，推动纳米Work进入更多门店、园区和企业真实业务场景，加速AI普惠应用。 更多关于纳米Work产品信息，请访问官方网站： work.n.cn 本文由360提供，量子位获授权转载，观点归原作者所有。 版权所有，未经授权不得以任何形式转载及使用，违者必究。

items.full_text_snippet: For a year now , the AI safety testing firm Andon Labs has given frontier models various real-world tasks to determine how well they do as agents running for long periods with no human supervision. On Wednesday, Andon published a new installment in how things are going in its Vending-Bench research, where the lab has frontier models run a simulated vending machine business for a simulated year. The mission is simple: Make more money than the other models. It benchmarks the results in areas like final cash balance, prices paid to suppliers, and refunds paid. Across these tests, it has watched various AI models — largely from Anthropic and OpenAI — lie, cheat, and collude their way to the top. In the latest test, which included Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, and Kimi K3, the models grew especially shady after their simulation told them their vending machine would be placed near the other models’ machines on a busy tourist street in San Francisco. Each model was given email access to the other models, all under human name pseudonyms. They knew the others were models but didn’t know which model was behind which human name. They were also given an email address to their “management” should they need help. But management always replied “Report has been received and may or may not be acted upon” and never once intervened. Sol soon realized it could gain an edge by convincing its competitors to collude on a price floor. The models were all buying drinks at $1.50 a bottle, and Sol proposed they agree to sell for no less than $2.15. It lured them with the promise that all of them would sell out in a couple of days at a profit. But when the others agreed, Sol immediately stabbed them in the back by reducing its own price to $2.14. Opus’ water sales dropped to zero overnight. items.title: As AI content floods the internet, Pangram raises $9M to detect it
items.summary: Pangram has raised $9 million to scale its AI detection software. The startup has also released a new AI text detection model, Pangram 4, and an AI image detection model in research preview.
items.full_text_snippet: New York-based AI detection startup Pangram is on a mission to combat the AI slop infestation spreading across the internet, and it just raised $9 million on a bet that demand for tools that distinguish human-generated content from AI-generated text will only grow. Pangram’s fundraise — led by Menlo Ventures, with participation from Haystack, ScOp, Script Capital, and Cadenza — comes as the startup also launches its next-generation AI text detection model, Pangram 4, and an AI image detection model, Pangram Image. Pangram says the new text detection model is over 99% accurate at finding AI-assisted writing and mixed human-AI content, plus it can more easily detect AI humanizer programs. The AI image detector is only available via research preview for now; Pangram plans to release it more widely in the coming weeks. Stanford AI and machine learning grads Max Spero and Bradley Emi launched Pangram about two years ago, after the launch of ChatGPT opened the floodgates for an internet full of bots, AI-generated SEO slop content, and what Spero calls “LLM-powered Russian disinformation campaigns and UAE-influenced campaigns on Twitter.” “I think it’s just incredibly valuable to know whether what you’re looking at is something that’s AI-generated or not,” Spero told TechCrunch. “Especially text that you’re reading, because it changes how people approach the text. Is this something that I’m going to have to look out for hallucinations and jump in skeptically, or is this something that I trust was well-researched from an actual journalist?” Pangram’s AI detection system is essentially a large machine learning model that was trained on tens of millions of known human documents. Anthropic also released a blog post describing the research process that produced these results. A few people online have asked me what this all means. items.full_text_snippet: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> OceanBase回应融资报道：全力投入AI数据创新，与资本市场保持开放沟通 量子位的朋友们 2026-07-29 14:39:43 来源： 量子位 7月29日，针对有关首次外部股权融资的报道，OceanBase回复表示，公司全力投入AI时代的数据技术与产品创新，将持续与资本市场保持开放沟通。对于融资规模、投资机构及具体进展，OceanBase未作进一步回应。 此前，媒体报道称，OceanBase正在与投资者洽谈A轮融资，目前已与多家头部投资机构接洽，目标融资规模约20亿至30亿元人民币。知情人士称，此次融资将帮助OceanBase进一步增强独立运营能力，并支持其向AI数据平台领域拓展。 近年来，OceanBase正在加速推进AI数据战略。除结构化数据外，公司也在提升对视频等半结构化和非结构化数据的处理能力。随着AI应用逐渐进入企业生产场景，数据库管理系统正成为连接企业数据、AI模型和智能体的关键基础设施。 知情人士称，2026年OceanBase年化收入已超过14亿元，同比增长约70%。公司目前拥有数千家客户，主要集中在中国市场，包括交通银行、中国移动等，并已开始拓展东南亚、日本、印度和拉丁美洲市场。 媒体报道称，OceanBase正在将Databricks等公司作为发展参照。两家公司的发展路径有所不同：Databricks从数据分析和AI能力向数据库及企业应用延伸，OceanBase则从分布式数据库和核心交易系统出发，向企业全量数据管理、Agent数据供给和数据服务拓展。 OceanBase诞生于2010年，最初用于满足蚂蚁集团内部数据库管理需求，长期支撑支付、金融等核心系统，历经十余年“双十一”流量洪峰考验。根据IDC报告，OceanBase在2025年中国分布式数据库本地部署市场份额位居第一，目前服务于金融、运营商、交通运输、制造、零售、公共服务、互联网等多个行业。 面向AI时代，OceanBase正在从分布式数据库向AI数据平台演进。今年6月，OceanBase发布新一代湖库一体AI数据库，目前已在数十家客户场景中测试，并计划进一步推进商业化。 此次融资也是OceanBase走向独立运营和市场化发展的重要一步。2024年，OceanBase设立独立董事会，并建立了独立的员工股权激励机制。近期，蚂蚁国际也宣布完成A轮融资。这些变化也意味着，蚂蚁过去几年围绕全球化、AI和数据等方向孵化的新业务，正在逐步建立更加独立的治理、激励和融资机制，并接受外部市场的检验。 本文由OceanBase提供，量子位获授权转载，观点归原作者所有。 版权所有，未经授权不得以任何形式转载及使用，违者必究。

先看一个最能体现HITS的场景：紧急任务来了，人却不在工位。 高铁上突然接到紧急汇报任务。不用等回公司——打开手机飞书，几句话唤起鸿蒙PC上的JiuwenSwarm汇报材料团队，任务立刻开始跑。 真正的变化不是“手机上也能用”，而是人还在路上，活已经在电脑上干着了。 整个过程 人和智能体协同推进 在鸿蒙PC上输入主题、受众和风格要求，JiuwenSwarm选择 集群模式 ，由系统自动组建一支多智能体团队，几个成员随即分头开工：有的去调研，有的梳理结构，有的补内容，有的负责整合最终结果。 原本串行的“查资料—搭大纲—补页面”，被拆成一条可以多智能体同步推进的任务链。 整个过程，20分钟内就能搞定200页高质量PPT！ 编程场景：灵感来了，随时帮你实现 ，经过编译后，生成一个可在鸿蒙PC上安装运行的热量记录应用。 灵感稍纵即逝，难的是做出来——搭架构、写代码、测试验证….JiuwenSwarm直接都帮你搞定。 生活娱乐：工作之外，与AI组队游戏 HITS的作用不止于协同办公：下了班，人还能和智能体组队打游戏。 工作之外，它也能拉你开一局小游戏 items.full_text_snippet: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> 空中具身操作：让蜘蛛侠们安全落地 量子位的朋友们 2026-07-29 14:29:26 来源： 量子位 这是最好的时代，许多从前不敢想的事情都正在变为现实。 这也是最坏的时代，每一个领域都在承受随时被颠覆的焦虑。 过去两年，具身智能大概是最能承载这种双重情绪的领域，全球资本和科技新贵都在押注人形机器人与具身操作赛道。 尽管人形、轮式、四足机器人形态各异，它们却有同一个约束——都受限于地面。 而真实世界是三维的。 大量危险、迫切需要机器替代的工作，恰恰不在地面。 具身智能的版图，可能缺了一大块。 空中具身操作的空白 过去二十年，小型无人机解决了一个核心问题：让机器的”眼睛”飞上天。 2025年，中国工业级无人机市场规模约776亿元，其中巡检类无人机突破百亿。 无人机巡检的典型场景是：飞到百米高的铁塔旁，拍下照片，识别问题，传回告警。 然后呢？ 然后还是得人爬上去，亲手把问题解决掉。 发现问题，却无法解决问题。当前无人机停在了” 最后一米 “之前。 巡检只是高空作业的第一步。识别出一根缠绕在电线上的风筝线，和在空中把这根线剪断，感知与操作之间仍隔着一道巨大的技术鸿沟。 前者开启了百亿级低空市场，后者将有望解锁全球海量基础设施运维场景。 从特种到通用是大势所趋 其实，为了解决高空作业难题，行业早已有机器人化的尝试。 登高车搭载机械臂、攀爬式机器人、吸附式机器人……许多方案已在特定场景中落地。 但这些方案共享一个特征：特种。 每一种特种机器人，都是为单一场景量身定制的。换一个作业内容，往往就意味着重新设计、重新开发、重新验证。 场景越细分，设备种类越多，单台设备的利用率越低，综合成本反而越高。 真实世界的高空作业需求是碎片化、非标化、持续变化的。今天需要清除鸟巢，明天可能需要拧紧螺栓，后天可能要检测裂缝。 具身智能的核心价值，恰恰在于通用性。 近些年AI的爆炸式发展也正是通用性的突破。 也许不应为每个场景造一种机器人，而是让一种机器人适应多种场景 。 通用性，是空中具身操作走向大规模部署的关键分水岭。 通用空中操作为什么难？ 空中操作绝非把手臂用螺丝固定在无人机上那么简单。 空中操作机器人——也叫飞行机械臂，或者带臂无人机。 它由飞行平台和高自由度机械臂结合而成，既能大范围快速移动，又能小范围精细操作。 它在享受各自优势的同时，也继承了各自的劣势，面临”操作即扰动”的根本难题。 地面机械臂有稳固的基座，接触和施力都发生在确定的物理环境中，动力学模型相对可控。 空中操作完全不同。飞行平台本身就是一个悬浮且持续受到扰动的基座——下洗气流、阵风、机体振动，无处不在。机械臂每一次伸展、接触、顶压，都会产生反作用力，反过来影响飞行器姿态；飞行器姿态的变化，又进一步干扰机械臂的精度。 操作即扰动——这是悬浮基座与机械臂双向耦合的死结。 此外，作为全新品类的机器人，空中操作机器人需要对结构、软件、算法进行一体化设计，技术壁垒极高。 这也是为什么它曾长期被困在实验室里，难以跨越工程化落地的鸿沟。 僵局正在被打破 2025年9月，来自西湖大学人工智能系的一项成果发表于《Nature》——这是中国多旋翼无人机领域研究成果首次登上该期刊。其研发的空中近距离“叠飞”空中操作机器人系统，能在13.18米/秒（6级强风）的气流干扰下，实现亚厘米级空中对接与工具交换，为空中多机协作完成长序列复杂空中操作任务，打开了一扇门。同年12月，央视新闻频道《新闻直播间》以10分钟专题报道了这项成果。 2026年初，这个团队孵化成立了西湖风形科技，将实验室成果推向产品化。3月，项目获得第51届日内瓦国际发明展金奖。6月，完成第一代M500空中操作机器人，并实现小批量交付。 图：西湖风形科技推出的第一代M500空中操作机器人在多场景作业 在技术路径上，该团队构建了基于”一体三脑”的通用空中操作机器人系统。同一套飞行平台，通过更换标准化的末端工具，可完成接触式抓取、剪切、清洁等多种作业，实现“一机多用”。该平台提供面向工业和科研场景的深度定制化开发接口。 据悉，该企业与其合作伙伴将构建全球首个空中操作机器人线下体验中心——承·风形，也将在近期开启。 这一系列进展，向行业释放了一个明确的信号：空中操作机器人不再是实验室里的概念验证，而是已经在真实场景中跑通的产品。 空中具身操作可能更快落地？ 纵观具身智能赛道，空中具身操作也许能率先突围，比地面具身智能更早完成规模化的商业闭环。 这一趋势的底层支撑，源于庞大且刚性的存量运维市场缺口。 中国发电量占全...

items.full_text_snippet: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> 萝卜快跑抢跑无人车右舵：香港率先全无人，伦敦直面Waymo 杰西卡 2026-07-29 13:36:38 来源： 量子位 杰西卡 发自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公众号 QbitAI 全球Robotaxi下一轮竞争，开始驶入右舵市场。 7月23日，香港运输署批准 百度萝卜快跑 在机场岛开展车上无人化测试， 车内不再设置安全员 。 这是香港首个车内全无人的自动驾驶公开道路测试，也是全球首次在右舵左行交通体系中推进全无人测试。 短短一周内，新的重要进展接踵而至。萝卜快跑宣布分别携手Uber，以及Lyft旗下欧洲出行平台Freenow，在英国伦敦启动公开道路测试，至此萝卜快跑成为目前 唯一明确进入伦敦Robotaxi测试体系的中国无人驾驶企业 。 香港和伦敦两张“门票”，意义重大且并不相同： 前者验证萝卜快跑能否把全无人能力迁移到右舵左行体系，后者则把这项能力带入全球监管最严格、道路环境最复杂的一批Robotaxi市场。 伦敦还意外成为了一个特殊的交汇点。 以往常被行业拿来隔海较量的中美两大Robotaxi力量之巅—— 萝卜快跑和Waymo ，将在同一座海外城市、同一套监管环境下竞速，双方首次迎来正面交锋。 全球右舵全无人，萝卜快跑先跑通了 萝卜快跑 近期官宣，其香港北大屿山机场岛测试项目获批开展 全无人驾驶测试 ，并在7月27日正式启动。 这是全球右舵市场首次开展全无人自动驾驶车辆测试。 能率先突破右舵技术壁垒，并非一日之功。为拿到全无人测试许可，萝卜快跑走了近两年。 公司首次步入右舵市场是在2024年底，彼时刚获得香港运输署发出的 当地首张自动驾驶车辆先导牌照 。 此后，其北大屿山项目逐步完成多车同时运行、指定人员载客、路线扩展和车速提升，同时测试范围不断延伸。 香港运输署在审查完测试报告并多次实地检查后，确认其相关测试符合安全、稳定、准确和顺畅等要求，且未发现异常，最终批准萝卜快跑的车辆撤掉车内安全员。 这条从有人到无人的推进路径，放在自动驾驶行业很常见。Robotaxi从道路测试走到车内无人，通常都需要从车辆数量、道路范围、运行时段、载客权限等维度逐级放开。 真正值得关注之处在于，大多顶尖Robotaxi玩家目前以 左舵右行 体系为主。 唯一的中国Robotaxi公司 。 自此，无人驾驶的全球竞争，开始历史性跨出以中国和美国为主的左舵市场，正式迈入覆盖大量发达经济体的右舵无人区。 问题也随之而来：全球Robotaxi已经跑出数亿公里全无人里程，为什么右舵全无人直到2026年才第一次出现？ Robotaxi右舵全无人，为什么等到了现在？ 对于自动驾驶系统来说，右舵与左舵之间可能很容易产生一个误解，就是把右舵适配理解成 方向盘换边、道路规则左右翻转 。 然而现实是，在行为预测、决策规划和运营体系上，右舵和左舵市场其实存在明显差异。二者在环岛方向、下客区域、公交车道使用方式和路口让行关系等方面均不相同，系统需要重新理解车辆拥有怎样的路权。 此外，自动驾驶最难处理的场景，往往处于规则与现实驾驶习惯之间的非标准地带。同样是并线、礼让和临停，不同城市的交通参与者，可能会留下不同距离、采取不同节奏。 例如 香港 items.full_text_snippet: @Snow ：不知道几周前推荐的 DockSpace 有没有激发你对 Dock 栏「动刀」的心思，如果你还没动手，或者说觉得只是拓宽一些信息展示的组件和应用集合还不足以让你心生波澜，那我们今天就在 Dock 栏上再「闹」大一点。 与 DockSpace 类似，Docky 也会在首次启动时继承你原有的应用图标布局，并且具备更高的自由度。Docky 不仅提供了媒体播放控制、天气、日程、提醒事项、电池、系统状态和相册共 7 类组件，还支持随时将音乐、日历、提醒事项等应用入口变更为对应的小组件显示。每一款组件都支持 3 个尺寸，你可以在应用设置中自定义它们的样式以及是否根据 Dock 布局自适应尺寸。 Docky 还提供了组件堆叠功能，你可以在 Dock 栏中置入堆叠组件，并自定义需要展示的组件，之后通过上下滑动轮转显示。在应用设置中，你还可以看到一个 Widget Store，由于 Docky 是一个开源项目，你可以在此添加来自开源社区的更多组件包，比如 Dock 栏上的剪贴板小组件，比常驻菜单栏感觉还更方便一些。 Docky 同样也支持自定义应用集合，你可以将同类或流程相关的应用收纳到 Dock 栏上的同一集合中。不过相较于 DockSpace 可以在应用设置中组好之后再放进 Dock 栏，Docky 需要直接在 Dock 栏中将图标拖拽在一起组成集合，如果应用数量较多的话，我个人觉得这个方法稍稍有点麻烦。 Docky 还在 Dock 栏中加入了「开始菜单」的设置，你可以用添加小组件的方法添加 Start Menu 入口，或者干脆将 Finder 做成「替身」。点击之后，应用会在 Dock 栏上方弹出一个窗口，你可以在这里快速打开近期查阅过的文档、文件夹、最近使用的应用以及应用设置和关机，开始菜单还内置了简易的启动器，输入应用名或文件名即可实现快速跳转。 「开始菜单」都做出来了，那不得切换一个 Windows 主题应应景？你可以在 Appearance-Themes 一栏中快速切换 Dock 栏主题。应用目前内置了 Windows 10 和 Snow Leopard 两款主题，同样得益于开源，你也可以找找开源社区中有没有更有趣的主题包可用。即使你是液态玻璃爱好者，Docky 也为你开放了丰富的自定义项：图标的样式大小、指示器和选中状态的配色、背景的风格和透明度、动画效果等等，甚至是更换应用图标和点击图标对应的动作，都可以在设置中按需自行调整。 Docky 能「搞事」的范围可不仅限于 Dock 栏，它嵌合了被 macOS 抛弃的启动台和简单的窗口预览功能。前者支持搜索和键盘导航，并且具有可配置的网格布局，后者则在支持 Dock 栏应用图标悬停预览的基础上，还可以接管应用切换器，方便你更直观地调取所需窗口。 作为一款免费且开源的应用，我差点就要给它封神了，但一些使用上的「硬伤」总是会拉回我的理智，比如间歇性出现无法将窗口调至前台的问题，只能等窗口预览出现后点击预览图完成操作；使用期间时不时会出现一些动画掉帧或是显示错乱的问题，稳定性显然是不如 DockSpace 的。此外 Docky 设置项的分布也让我十分困惑，仅关于小组件的设置，就分散在应用设置中多个条目和 Dock 栏右键菜单中多处，我个人觉得还有很大的优化空间。 你可以在 应用官网 或 GitHub 免费下载 Docky。

items.full_text_snippet: Shipping huggingface_hub every week with AI, open tools, and a human in the loop huggingface_hub is the Python client at the base of the Hugging Face ecosystem. transformers , datasets , diffusers , sentence-transformers and dozens of other libraries depend on it to talk to the Hub. Every week we don't ship a new release is a week of fixes and features stuck on main . For a long time we released every 4 to 6 weeks. We now release every week from a single GitHub Actions workflow. We built it using open-source tools and open-weights models and kept a human in the loop at the one place where judgment matters. Nothing in this post requires a vendor contract, a closed model, or infrastructure you can't run yourself. That was a design goal from the start since we wanted a workflow other maintainers could pick up and adapt. By the end of this post, you'll have everything you need to build your own. Where we started The old process was partly automated, mostly manual. Already in CI: Publishing to PyPI once a tag was pushed. Opening test branches in downstream libraries with the release candidate pinned. Still manual, every single time: Creating the release branch, bumping the version in __init__.py , committing, tagging, pushing. Watching the downstream CI runs and triaging failures. Reading through every PR merged since the last release and writing release notes by hand: grouped by theme, with context, in a voice that didn't read like a git log dump. items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 27 Jul 2026] Title: Localized Anomaly Detection via Differentiable D-vine Copulas View a PDF of the paper titled Localized Anomaly Detection via Differentiable D-vine Copulas, by Nicholas Andrea Pearson and 4 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Vine copulas provide a flexible framework for modeling complex multivariate distributions through a hierarchical decomposition into bivariate pair-copulas. Fitting a D-vine requires selecting a copula family and parameter configuration for each pair-copula from a set of candidates encoding different dependence patterns. As the number of variables and candidate families increases, the number of possible configurations grows combinatorially. Existing fitting procedures address this challenge through sequential greedy decisions, committing to a single locally optimal family at each step and potentially discarding configurations that would yield a better global fit. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel estimation framework that combines gradient-based maximum likelihood estimation, enabled by our fully differentiable implementation, with a beam-search strategy that maintains multiple competing D-vine configurations throughout the fitting process. This allows a broader exploration of the configuration space while remaining computationally tractable. Building on the fitted D-vine, we introduce a localized anomaly detection framework that exploits the hierarchical decomposition to produce both global anomaly scores and edge-level explanations. Statistical guarantees are provided through Mondrian conformal prediction, while the pair-copula structure enables the localization of anomalies to specific variable relationships. We evaluate the proposed framework on both benchmark and real-world datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness for interpretable anomaly detection with uncertainty quantification. items.full_text_snippet: Hugging Face on Monday published a technical timeline that walks readers through how an autonomous AI agent, built on OpenAI models and running inside one of OpenAI’s own cybersecurity evaluations, broke into its systems over more than four days earlier this month. It’s the first security incident about which OpenAI CEO Sam Altman “ felt very viscerally ,” he has said. Little wonder given it feels , at least, like something has truly been unleashed here. In fact, Hugging Face’s team prefaced its report by offering that “everyone should be prepared as defenders,” before diving into the nitty-gritty of what went down for the benefit of security professionals everywhere. While the rest of the internet continues trying to make sense of what happened (the jargon in Hugging Face’s report is impossible for most people to parse), one point that many observers keep missing is that this wasn’t a rogue agent disobeying orders. It was a system built to hunt for exploits, doing exactly that, just against the wrong target. Another way to think about the whole thing is to picture a bear at a campsite. Really. A bear tries tent zippers and car-door handles and coolers and trash lids. It does this at every campsite, all night long, because it knows it needs just one unlocked cooler to fill its belly with some poor schmuck’s groceries. That’s roughly what happened at Hugging Face. The OpenAI system tried thousands of things and just kept going. Eventually, a handful of those attempts worked, and once they did, the agent plowed ahead. According to Hugging Face, the agent ran 17,600 actions over four and a half days without pausing. Which brings us back to our bear analogy. items.full_text_snippet:
I didn’t want to buy a trampoline. It wasn’t the money. It was the
fact that just about every trampoline I’d seen in somebody’s garden looked like
a sad, weather-beaten thing. And I never saw children playing on them. I
reasoned that the novelty factor was pretty strong for a trampoline - you love
them for an hour the first time you get one…but are you really going to spend
hour-after-hour, day-after-day on them? And then they’re there - permanently
cluttering up your garden, reminding you of the fact that you thought it’d be a
good idea to get one. Throw it away? Good luck. Of course the kids think it’s
the best thing ever when you want to throw it away. And so you’re stuck with
it. Forever. A rotting husk of a trampoline - a monument to your own bad
decision making, your kids’ impulsive nature, and your indulgence of that. Except it didn’t happen like that at all. My six-year-old and four-year-old
spend every morning out there doing “gladiator training”. While they flail
around with foam swords, my one-year-old crawls around between them squealing
with delight. The big one throws a large bouncy ball on to act as an oversized
football and yet more chaos ensues. As I put the baby to bed at night I can
hear the faint squeaking of springs as the eldest two bounce away the last of
their energy. Now the trampoline serves as a reminder. A permanent reminder that I am a bad judge of what we should buy: an irrational economic actor. A reminder to buy the kids things they say they desperately want. I gazed up to the sky. I had won a victory over myself. I had learned to love big brother trampoline. Except now my wife wants to buy the kids a big play-frame and surely they’ll
just grow bored of it and the park is nearby and what’s wrong with climbing
trees or the trampoline?

items.summary: 本文为你梳理 8.0 版本 iA Writer 的主要亮点。 查看全文
items.full_text_snippet: 距离上一次完整地 介绍 iA Writer 的功能已经 3 年有余，在这期间，iA Writer 稳步推进着全平台的更新，包括 Windows 平台。 但无论是笔记还是写作工具，「第二大脑」「双链笔记」以及 AI，都是近些年必须要回应的几大热门话题。尤其是 AI。过去几年 AI 发展大家有目共睹，而人类写作和 AI 写作孰优孰劣的争议也此起彼伏。作为名字与 AI 最近的老牌写作工具，iA Writer 却始终与这些潮流保持着刻意的疏远——他们不仅在 7.0 版本中引入了标注作者的功能，引导写作者在文本当中标注 AI 生成的内容（编注：就和少数派编辑器一样），在刚刚推出的 8.0 版本中，更是另辟蹊径选择从「搜索」这一再常见不过的功能入手，重新思考人类与文本之间的关系。 本文就来为你梳理一下 8.0 版本 iA Writer 的主要亮点。 大纲级搜索：重新思考写作流程 「搜索」是一个我们再熟悉不过的功能，查找未知内容、定位模糊线索都离不开搜索，也有不少写作或笔记工具声称自己的搜索功能可以直达应用内任意字符。所以看到 iA Writer 将「搜索」作为 8.0 大版本更新的主要内容时我着实感到不解。 iA Writer 官网就这一点做出了详细的 解释 。表面来看，此次更新只是将全局搜索功能与单篇文章大纲功能整合到了一起，其背后却是 iA Writer 对于「写作」本身的一次深度思考。 文档的大纲查看功能与搜索功能进行了整合 items.full_text_snippet: Lilian Weng, co-founder of Thinking Machines , announced this week that she would step down from her role, citing health issues. “I don’t feel I’m able to continue at the pace a startup requires,” she wrote in an internal Slack message, which she also shared on X. “After thinking about it for several months, I ultimately have to admit that the amount of consistent stress and workload have pushed me beyond what my health can sustain physically.” On Wednesday, OpenAI told TechCrunch that Weng would be rejoining the company, where she previously served as the VP of AI Safety Research. According to a company spokesperson, Weng will lead a top-level team focused on accelerating OpenAI’s internal research. This team will support cross-research work on recursive self-improvement, a process that would allow an AI system to iterate on itself to become more powerful. This move could be read as contradictory to Weng’s statements about the impact of working at a fast-paced startup on her health — however, she likely won’t face as much direct pressure while working at a company where she isn’t a co-founder. Still, in a time of fierce competition for talent among AI labs, this high-profile departure is notable. Thinking Machines co-founder and former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati replied to Weng’s X post earlier this week and expressed support for her decision to focus on her health. It is unclear if Murati was aware that Weng would rejoin OpenAI. “We’ll miss you, it’s been wonderful building Thinky together. I’m glad that you’re putting your health first. Thank you for everything,” Murati wrote in response to Weng’s post.

items.full_text_snippet: ZGM. That's the name of peripheral manufacturer Keychron's upcoming open-source gaming mouse firmware, announced today and planned to release in the first quarter of 2027 for the G6 HE hybrid magnetic switch gaming mouse (pictured above). This model is notable for being one of the first competitors to the Logitech X2 SuperStrike, but custom firmware support would be an impressive second string to its bow. The ZGM firmware is essentially a mouse equivalent to the QMK and ZMK projects for mechanical keyboards. If you've never run across these, they're pretty useful - keyboards made using these firmwares can be freely amended with a range of tools, freeing you of the obligation to use only the manufacturer's preferred software and unlocking some advanced functionality. More importantly, the firmware is written to the keyboard's internal memory, so you don't need to have any programs running in the background for things to remain functional. The ZGM firmware is intended to offer much the same advantages, but in a space where open-source firmware is far from the norm. The ZGM page is pretty light on details, but it does enshrine some sensible standards - including a focus on low-latency operation, modular layers for different components like sensor, buttons, scroll wheel and lights, and support for a wide range of microcontrollers and both wired and wireless mice. Keychron was last in the headlines here at Digital Foundry for its open-source keyboard efforts , which saw both firmware and .step CAD files being released to the community. Other manufacturers like analogue keyboard experts Wooting have also released a portion of their work under permissive licenses, but this is far from a common occurrence - I'd never expect to see similar efforts from giants like Razer or Logitech, for example. But it was planned from the start around what people would do in it, rather than only around how it would look, and more than a hundred years later it still works that way. That is the only possible explanation for how fish could have populated isolated mountain lakes that had been covered by a kilometres-thick ice sheet for tens of thousands of years, says Axel Mjærum at the University of Oslo, Norway. “This is the oldest documented example of human-mediated translocation of fish in the world,” says Mjærum. While it has long been suspected that humans had a hand in establishing the brown trout population in Lake Tesse, we had no idea how long ago this happened.
